title: Why every company now needs to think and operate like a lab team | Josh Woodward (VP Google Labs)
summary: Google Labs head on running a frontier team: shrinking product teams, blurring but not merging roles, prototype-and-watch validation, rolling six-month planning, and why model benchmarks are overhyped.

assertions.quote: most people in the world are never ever ever going to care about an ELO rating
in practice it's not that much different than the previous model that also everyone thought was the best model ever
We used to say like it's about five to seven people. Now it's about two to three people.
strategy and ops people and BD people and marketing people, you know, kind of be like builders in labs and they are really good
we talk a lot about how do we get outside the building and just show people prototypes
as the execution cost of making products goes down we'll be able to make more products
I still feel like collaboration and like how you work with people matters even more now.
all these model capabilities and benchmarks and all the intelligence gets translated into just like can you build something people want
trending towards like you being able to direct lots of agents and not having to work with as many people
people are maybe overhyping like everybody's a builder and it's just this new job function and everything's kind of the same

verdicts.note: A framing of how teams should value skills; no measurement would settle it.

Internal survey, interviews and Claude Code usage data at Anthropic show teams using Claude for their core tasks and also to work outside their expertise (backend engineers building UIs, security analysing unfamiliar code), so 'everyone becomes more full-stack'; it supports the cross-role half but does not test whether specialist expertise stays each person's primary value, and it is a single-company self-report.

assertions.quote: that we think about planning is kind of almost like rolling six months

verdicts.note: Practice advice about planning cadence whose fit depends on the organization.

assertions.quote: a team, however you want to manifest it, that is their job is to be at the frontier

verdicts.note: Organizational advice; corporate-lab history offers anecdotes for and against, not a measurable test.
